_help.about: The biome gate (design 1 Oct §CA, Mike: a species belongs in its natural environment; a savanna is acacias, grass and shrubs). VegetationPlacer placed by climate bands alone, so a floodplain-forest magnolia grew on a savanna riverbank. Now a species grows only in a biome whose file lists it (plants, or an association's dominant / companion / ground / catalogue) and, for a data/plants catalogue entry, only in the biomes its own `biomes` list names. Climate, soil, altitude, needs and the realm gate (§AA) still apply inside those biomes. Restart after editing.
_help.biome_gate: true: the gate is on. false: the old rule (bands only) — for A/B only.
_help.catalogue_needs_biomes: true: a data/plants entry with no `biomes` list does not grow (like an untagged realm) until the fill tags it. false: untagged catalogue entries grow wherever a biome file copies them.
_help.ecotone_m: A neighbouring biome's species may cross the border this far into a biome that does not list them, when their own bands fit. 0: hard borders (Mike, 1 Oct: a gallery forest is a floodplain-forest cell, not a bleed). Open it later if the borders look fake.
_help.association_lists_count: Which lists in a biome's associations count as 'listed' for the gate.
_help.walkabout: tools/walkabout.gd, the end-of-pass check (§CA): seeds, sites per seed, hours, first-person eye height, how far it looks, and that any species in an unlisted biome fails it. Frames and the species list are the report; the dev frame is for grade measurements only.
_help.trim: Design 1 Oct §CC (Mike): the catalogue is trimmed to archetypes. Ten categories (tree, shrub, grass, moss, orchid, aroid, fern, cacti, fungi, vine; cacti added 12:04, vine 14:04); each biome keeps at most per_biome_per_category species per category, and only where the biome has that category at all (a hot desert has no moss; the open ocean has no tree); nothing is invented to fill a slot. The four are chosen from seed_list first (Mike's list, 12:08: a name is kept if it is a real accepted binomial, native to that kind of place and drawable at the player's eye, and is ADDED with the full PLANT_SCHEMA blocks if the catalogue lacks it), then the biome file's dominants and companions, then what a flora of that place names first. never_drawable: kinds of organism that are never kept. The special catalogues in keep_whole stay as they are. Every other data/plants catalogue file is folded into the biome lists it serves or archived to archive_dir. category_of maps the schema's shape / tier vocabulary onto the nine categories; an entry that fits none (kelp, a cushion plant, a lichen) is archived unless it is the biome's hero_species or in always_keep. A hero species always survives. always_keep: the always_present groups (§CE) — never trimmed, whole, whatever the per-category cap.
_help.always_present: Design 1 Oct §CE (Mike: make sure these are in the game — Musa, Amorphophallus, Cannabis, Trichocereus, Acacia, bamboo, vines). A group is matched by genus, shape, name or trim category. Two guarantees: (1) the trim (§CC) never cuts a member (trim.always_keep names these groups); (2) presence: in the stand roll (§BH) a member that fits the site (climate, soil, biome gate, realm gate) is always an ASSOCIATE, never left in the accent pool, and each group present in a chunk gets at least min_share of its tier's stems there, split among its fitting members. one_roll_per_binomial: entries sharing a binomial (the 64 cannabis landraces are one species, Cannabis sativa) roll as ONE species; the local landrace is then the fitting entry nearest in climate and realm. no_terpene_evidence 'accent_only' (Mike, 2 Oct: "we won't have that much Japanese hemp because there's no evidence of terpene relevance"): a member whose catalogue entry says cannabis.terpene_evidence 'none' (Japanese hemp) still grows where it fits, but only as a scattered accent: never lifted, never a stand's dominant or associate. tools/plant_presence_check.gd is the check (full planet). Added 1 Oct night (§CM, Mike: there should be rhododendron forests, where mad honey comes from): the rhododendron group (genus Rhododendron).
_help.communities: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CS] Plants live in communities, and every community has one home (Mike, 3 Oct). spawn_as_community: a plant grows only as a member of a community (an association: its dominant, companion, ground and catalogue lists); the community places as a group, and each member still sits where its own bands, soil, light, water and nest fit. solo_by_numbers false: nothing places on its climate numbers alone. home one_land: before the player plants anything (§CT), each community is native to one land (a RealmMap province) and grows nowhere else; each land's stretch of a biome gets its own community, and no community repeats in two lands. deal_by niche: a community's home is a land where its niche exists (niche_keys), dealt by the seed, not by Earth's map. keep_lands_coherent: communities from the same part of Earth are dealt together where they fit, so a land keeps one character (Claude's call; the designer may prefer a free mix). catalogue_via_community: a catalogue species grows only through the communities that list it; until the data fill attaches it, unattached_catalogue keeps its current placement and the check lists it. short_biome: where a biome is in more lands than it has communities, the extra stretch takes the community of the nearest land that has one (it spread across the border) until a fill adds real communities; the check lists the short biomes. player_planted_exempt: what the player plants (§CT) is not bound to a home.

category_of.tree: canopy or emergent tier; shapes broadleaf, conifer, cypress, palm, umbrella (woody); tree ferns go to fern
category_of.shrub: shrub tier, woody; sagebrush, heath, mangrove seedling, bamboo thicket
category_of.grass: grasses, sedges, rushes, reeds, cattail, bamboo grasses; the ground tier's graminoids
category_of.fungi: fungi.json and any ground entry that is a mushroom, bracket, puffball or lichen-as-fungus
category_of.fern: ferns, tree ferns, whisk ferns, selaginella
category_of.aroid: aroids: Alocasia, Colocasia, Philodendron, Monstera, Bucephalandra, skunk cabbage, taro; Amorphophallus stays its own catalogue
category_of.cacti: cacti and the other stem succulents a desert flora groups with them: saguaro, cardon, prickly pear, barrel, cholla, Madagascar ocotillo, euphorbia candelabra; Trichocereus stays its own catalogue
category_of.vine: climbers and creepers: lianas, rattans, grapes, ivy, Virginia creeper, passion vines, pothos, climbing aroids (Monstera, Philodendron), climbing fern, morning glory, Gloriosa — the species that cover trunks, ruins, rock and ground (§CE)
